definitions.bytes: every HTTP request the driver sends and every response it receives, counted at the client side as they go over the socket: request line + header lines + blank line + body once the socket has taken them (a request whose connection is refused counts 0); status line + header lines + blank line + body as read from it. Each call is attributed to (the party that makes it, found from X-M2M-Origin; the endpoint it is sent to)
definitions.edge_cloud: a call that joins the two sides: a party at the edge calling the IN-CSE, or a party in the cloud calling an edge CSE (cse-mn-a, cse-mn-b, the MEC 011 of district A); plus the notifications a CSE on one side sends to a client's endpoint on the other
definitions.retargeted: a call sent to the IN-CSE with an SP-relative or absolute address of an edge CSE: one call, its bytes as the client counted them added once to edge-cloud and once to the IN-CSE; the IN-CSE's own hop to the edge is not seen by the client and not counted. This driver sends none
definitions.notifications: each request a CSE sends to /fl/<client> and the listener's answer, as read and written at the listener; attributed to (the CSE holding the orchestrator's <tasks>, the client)
definitions.harness: CAdmin's topology, leftover and cleanup checks, the removal of a leftover AE of an earlier run (sent under that AE's own originator, so no admin right is used) and the MEC 011 liveness and listing probes: counted per CSE, never edge-cloud
definitions.unmapped: a call whose originator is in no table: not the harness; counted at the CSE it was sent to, listed by name, never edge-cloud (its side is not known), and it makes the FL_03 recording step fail
definitions.per_cse: whole run: calls by the endpoint they were sent to, notifications by the CSE that sent them
definitions.round_bytes: the calls and notifications made inside run_round, from the orchestrator's discovery to the deletion of the temporary copies
definitions.round_time: time.monotonic_ns from just before the round's first task is sent to the orchestrator's <tasks> to the 201 for the new global model in the orchestrator's <model> (the redistribution), in whole microseconds; a round that published no model has none
definitions.median: over the rounds of one run that have a round time; of an even number, the mean of the middle two, rounded down
definitions.caveat: one PC, loopback: this is bytes counted at the client, not a network measurement (no packet capture, nothing below HTTP, 'edge' and 'cloud' are ports on one host); the round time on loopback says little about real latency
